pairs.question: Ego debeo accipere ab illo similitudinem?
pairs.answer: Alexander in omnibus peritissimus est et in nullo offendit, omnia ipse faciens viriliter; formam et virtutem secundum suam nativitatem leonis habet.
pairs.derivation: Darius asks whether he should take an example from Alexander; the satrap (Cui alius satrapas dixit) answers describing Alexander's excellence and lion-like nature. Dropped the speech tag 'Cui alius satrapas dixit'. Answer ends at the full stop after 'leonis habet'; what follows is Darius's next question 'Unde tibi hoc cognitum?', a new exchange.

pairs.question: Unde tibi hoc cognitum?
pairs.answer: Quando perrexi per tuam iussionem Macedoniam tollere censum Philippo patri suo, vidi eum et cognovi sapientiam illius et figuram eius intellexi.
pairs.derivation: Darius asks how the satrap knows this; the satrap (Cui ille) answers that he saw Alexander when sent to collect tribute from Philip. Dropped speech tag 'Cui ille'. Answer ends at first full stop ('intellexi'); what follows ('Quod si tibi placet, congrega omnes satrapas...') turns to advice, not an answer.

pairs.question: O strenue vir, quid est hoc?
pairs.answer: Ne estimes me, dominator, Macedonam esse, sed Persarum. Et ego promisi Dario venire, aufferre caput tuum; spopondit enim mihi dare in coniugio filiam suam et regales provintias.
pairs.derivation: Alexander asks the captured Persian assassin what this is; the Persian (Cui Persa barbarus dixit) answers explaining he is Persian and was sent by Darius to take Alexander's head. Dropped speech tag 'Cui Persa barbarus dixit'. Answer runs to end of his utterance; what follows is narration ('Tunc Alexander iussit...').

pairs.question: Quis es tu?
pairs.answer: Apochrisarius sum regis Alexandri missus ad te, dicens tibi, quia: moram facit exire preliari in campo cum inimicis suis; timidus est atque pavidus.
pairs.derivation: Darius asks the disguised Alexander who he is; Alexander (Cui ille) answers that he is the envoy of king Alexander. Dropped speech tag 'Cui ille'. Answer ends at 'pavidus'; what follows ('Unde si tibi placet, constitue diem preliandi') is a request, not part of the identification. Chose the Darius exchange (clear single asker/answerer) over the earlier corrupt '[Quis es tu?]' bracketed by the Persians at the gate.

pairs.question: O fortissime vir, quid est hoc, quod agis? Quare abscondis vasa aurea in sinu tuo?
pairs.answer: Noster senior sedens in convivio donat militibus suis vascula, cum quibus bibunt.
pairs.derivation: Darius asks why Alexander is hiding the golden cups; Alexander (Cui Alexander) answers that their lord gives soldiers the cups they drink with. Dropped speech tag 'Erexit se Darius et dixit' (narration of the asking) and 'Cui Alexander'. Answer ends at full stop ('bibunt'); what follows is narration of the guests' reaction.
